description: Cost ordering (for the user): intra-ASEAN shipping costs at least 11.42 EUR/t (chain at zero distance) + the receiver's sequestration 30 EUR/t (PyPSA-Eur default, research.s2.co2.sequestration_cost_eur_per_t) = 41.42 EUR/t, above the extra-ASEAN price 40.75 EUR/t (decision 89: IEAGHG chain at 4,500 km + ZEP 2011 offshore saline aquifer Medium 16.05 EUR2020/t). description: Decision 92: route factor port-to-port sea distance / great-circle distance = 1.091 (median over 503 candidate pairs; quartiles 1.0332 / 1.3075, p90 1.825), derived from the model geometry: shortest over-water paths on a 0.05 degree grid outside the ASEAN land of the author country shapes (grid bias on straight over-water pairs 1.0096); no published factor at hand and none in the S4D download category; first-batch sensitivity +-25 %

Decision 92: candidate shipping pairs (504): origin coastal buffered node, receiver, landing node (shortest sea path), great-circle km between the buses (used with the route factor), sea-path km (reference: pair-specific alternative), ratio, nearest-by-great-circle landing for reference

Decision 92 (revised): decisions 18 and 44 cut only cross-border network infrastructure when not interconnected; maritime trade stays in both scenarios and the value of interconnection comes from lines and pipelines only. CO2 shipping is maritime trade like the liquid fuels: links carry border_class = maritime_trade, are not removed by the cross-border switches and are not counted by B5 (network components only)

Decision 92: for every coastal buffered node of country i and every other country j with a national injection cap > 0, one link '<node> co2 ship to <j>' from '<node> co2 stored' to 'co2 sequestered <j>' (enters j's national store: occupies j's annual cap, decision 28, and pays j's store unit cost; the export counts as abatement of i, decision 20 - it leaves i's captured-CO2 buffer and enters no atmosphere); landing node = coastal node of j with the shortest sea path (CO2_SHIP_ROUTES_S4D2.csv); both scenarios
